subtype: Approach: asking a parent to hold the device [Action]
passage: Emil had noticed something: once the tablet was in his hand, homework stopped. On Sunday evening in their Oslo flat he carried it to the kitchen. "Mamma, can you keep this from four to six? I will ask for it back after." His mother raised her eyebrows. "Whose idea is this?" "Mine. I cannot stop once I start." She slid it into the drawer with the spare keys. At four Emil opened his reader, and his eyes strayed to the drawer only twice. His little brother Diego asked for a turn with it, and Mamma said no. At six Emil got the tablet back, homework done, and played without a worry.

qa.q: Where did Emil's mother put the tablet?
qa.a: She put it in the drawer with the spare keys.

qa.q: What did Emil realise about himself, and what did he want as a result?
qa.a: He realised he could not stop once he started, so he felt determined to get his mother's help to stay on track, and he chose it himself.

qa.q: What could Emil do if his mother is away one evening?
qa.a: He could put the tablet in another room himself and set a timer, because distance and a limit still help when she is not there.

qa.q: How might Mamma feel when Emil asks for this himself?
qa.a: Probably surprised and proud, since she asked whose idea it was and he answered that it was his. 🙂

grounding: A boy who finds it hard to stop asks his mother to hold the tablet during study hours, a limit he chose himself.
